findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 (htihle.github.io/weirdml.html, retrieved 2026-10-27) heads 'WeirdML v3', describes 11 tasks, and lists 'Previous versions: WeirdML v2 · WeirdML v1'. The row claims version "2", version_status "published", version_guard 'Verify the published version 2 before reading results.' The current published release is v3, not v2.
findings.repair: Adopt the current published version (3) and re-derive all version-dependent fields from the current protocol text; a changed task set and release version cannot silently reuse the existing identity.

findings.evidence: Row metric claims 'Average Max Accuracy: per task, mean over runs of the maximum test accuracy across the 5 iterations per run, averaged over all 17 tasks'. SOURCE 1's Scoring text defines the official score as 80% normalized area under the best-so-far effective-score curve on a log token axis (500k-50M) plus 20% of the final value, over 11 tasks / 15 configurations, and states effective scores 'are not raw accuracy'. The 17-task count also conflicts with the page's 11 tasks.
findings.repair: Replace the metric with the current protocol's stated scoring rule and task count; do not carry the claimed v2 scoring wording forward.

findings.evidence: Row description: 'unusual machine-learning tasks where they must write, run, and iteratively improve PyTorch code under fixed compute and time limits'. SOURCE 1 describes v3 as '11 complex hand-made tasks' about exploring and understanding unfamiliar data and building ML/data-analysis pipelines. The packet contains no v2 protocol excerpt, so the row's description cannot be confirmed for v2 and mismatches the current protocol.
findings.repair: Re-transcribe the description from the current primary protocol text when the version fix (f1) is applied.

uncertainties: Owner-side hash recomputation and transport/qualification checks were not executed by this reviewer; this is a stated limitation, not absent numeric source evidence.

Scale check (c1): SOURCE 3 shows 162 served avg_acc values, min 1.729411764705882, max 93.57264705882352, consistent with the row's unit 'percent' and range [0,100]; per the criteria this settles only the served scale, not metric meaning or provenance, so it does not offset f1/f2.

Lifecycle check (c2): SOURCE 2 (2 changed avg_acc values today) affirmatively supports status 'active'; the protocol's 'Previous versions' note alone is not a retirement, and no separate successor board is named, so c2 fields were not independently failed. They must be re-evaluated together with the version fix in f1.

Whether weirdml_data.csv serves the v2 or v3 payload cannot be determined from the packet; the field name 'avg_acc' matches the row's claimed accuracy metric rather than the v3 AUC-based scoring text, but the CSV is generated-capture summary evidence only.
